name: ExaSearchBot
follows_en: Yes, vendor says it checks robots.txt before fetching

ips.note: The vendor says every request is cryptographically signed with HTTP Message Signatures (Web Bot Auth) and gives a public key directory to verify against, and that verification holds regardless of IP address.

vendor_quote: Exa is a search engine. Similar to other search engines, Exa uses a robot (ExaSearchBot) to discover and index pages on the public web.
what_en: ExaSearchBot is the crawler of Exa, a search engine. Exa says its purpose is search and retrieval, so pages become discoverable and can be cited. Pages Exa fetches on a user's request rather than by crawling go out as ExaUser.
block_en: Exa says User-agent: ExaSearchBot with Disallow: / blocks ExaSearchBot from the whole site. If there is no ExaSearchBot group, it follows the rules set for major search engines, otherwise the * group. The vendor says robots.txt controls crawling, not indexing, so already indexed pages are removed with a noindex meta tag or X-Robots-Tag header.
compare_en: Both are search-index crawlers that feed AI answers with cited sources; ExaSearchBot signs its requests with Web Bot Auth and falls back to major search engines' rules when it has no group of its own.
notes: ExaUser (user-triggered fetch) has its own page at https://crawler.exa.ai/exauser; not read or covered here. Key directory not fetched; no IP list published on the page.
answer_en: ExaSearchBot is the crawler of Exa, a search engine built for search and retrieval, so pages can be discovered and cited. Exa says it checks robots.txt before fetching and that User-agent: ExaSearchBot with Disallow: / blocks the whole site. Every request is cryptographically signed, so verification does not depend on an IP address.
